question: Does one declarative property definition, consumed by reading, attribution, interpretation and comparability, recover the meaning of observations (property, condition dimensions, basis) better than the current mechanisms, in categories whose definitions were not written for them?

E1.material: S87b corpus (472 observations, 922 conditions) with the sealed S87b blind annotation (condition classes, measurand kind and basis)
E1.status: spent: used by S87b (dev and first check run); never held-out. Definitions author (Claude) had seen S87b aggregate results.

E2.material: same 472 observations; NEW blind Claude-agent reference of property attribution (definition label set or none) and condition dimension (or none), sealed before any scoring
metrics: property: correct, wrong, abstained, false attribution where the reference says none
four-set rule vs S87b class mechanism at class level

E3.material: 12 retained S80 pages, S86b sealed page reference (125 measured results)
compare: plan whose measurements are compiled from definitions (definitionPlanMeasurements), outcomes inherited
metrics: S86c scorer: measured results recovered, false readings

E4.material: unseen categories: definitions authored from owner packages BEFORE their documents are read; fresh pages under the research policy (robots, rights, private retention)
metrics: as E2 on a new sealed reference

groups.report: overall, per category, per group, worst group; development and check separately

stopRule: at most three reformulations of definitions or interpreter on development groups; then freeze and run check once; first check runs committed unchanged
